Unrolled K=10 TV-GD with per-iter learnable step+lambda (20 trainable scalars), supervised-L2 vs clean truth, init from LD-FBP. SEEDED from the sibling classical tv_iterative iter-1 corner (SSIM 0.92298 / hr 0.133): tv_step_init=0.01 (=classical tv_lr), tv_lambda_init=0.001 (=classical tv_lambda), tv_clip_max=0.05. ADDS a SHORT supervised training phase (train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1) on top of the 214-slice val pass. BUDGET (HARD 20 min train+score): classical tv_iterative ran 120 GD-iters x 214 slices in 918s (~0.036 s/slice-iter, dominated by the 2304-view 512px projector pair). This variant: val = K=10 unrolled x 214 slices, val_chunk=5 -> ~80-120s. Train = 40 samples x 8 epochs x K=10 x (fwd+bwd, ~2-3x a val slice-iter) ~ 256-380s. + 214-slice FBP precompute + load ~120s. Total ~7-10 min, ~2x margin under the 1200s wall. bs=1 holds only one K-step autograd graph at a time (memory-safe on 16 GB; no OOM risk vs the hammernik bs=4 OOM). FAILURE MODES TO AVOID: (a) 214-slice TV recon x training blows the wall -> kept K, train_n, epochs conservative; (b) under-training the 20 scalars -> epochs=8 gives the learnable step/lambda schedule room to depart from the seed while still fitting. HYPOTHESIS: a LEARNED per-iter lambda schedule lands at or slightly ABOVE the classical fixed-lambda tv_iterative hr 0.133, because the supervised end-to-end fit can adapt the data-vs-TV balance per unrolled step rather than holding one fixed lambda. If it under-performs the classical baseline, the K=10 unrolled depth (vs classical 120 iters) is the limiter and iter-2 raises tv_K.

ONE KNOB CHANGED: tv_K 10 -> 30 (3x deeper unroll). In reality a large slice of 321.5s is FIXED overhead (data load + 214-slice FBP precompute + per-ps probe ~60-120s), so the true K=30 cost is well under 964s. bs=1 holds only ONE K-step autograd graph at a time -> deeper K raises activation memory linearly but stays memory-safe on 16 GB (no OOM; cf. the hammernik bs=4 OOM). FALSIFIER: if SSIM/hr stay low at K=30, the limiter is NOT depth but the supervised-TV TRAINING (e.g. broken target/loss/optimisation), and iter-3 must check the training path (loss curve, learned step/lambda trajectory) rather than deepening further.
